answer: Each agent can earn a reputation only through tasks whose results are checked by randomly selected peers with established stake; a new identity starts with no history and cannot certify itself. To amplify influence, an attacker must fund many independent accounts and keep enough stake exposed that dishonest reviews can be slashed when later audits catch them. Splitting one account into onyx, marble, and mesa identities therefore multiplies capital and audit risk, not credibility; the mechanism raises the cost of a sybil swarm without claiming to make it impossible.
